newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly higher after paring some gains.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly higher after paring some gains.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Wednesday, but the upside was capped as Tokyo share prices rose off lows in the afternoon, traders said.
Concern about a possible rise in interest rates has waned considerably, and speculation that investors will want to increase their bond holdings is supporting JGBs, they said.
JGBs are likely to be unaffected if the U.S. Federal Reserve decides to leave interest rates unchanged, as expected, at its Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
The September ended at 124.50, up slightly from Tuesday's close of 124.36. Turnover was 38,494 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.320 percent as of 0707 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday's close.

JGBs lost some upward momentum in the afternoon session as cash bonds were sold after Tokyo share prices managed to claw back above the key 20,000 point level, an analyst for a major brokerage house said.
"The fall below the 20,000 level had made it hard to sell JGBs, but when they (stocks) rose back above it, cash JGBs such as the 182nd issue were sold," he said.

JGBs rose in the morning session due to a variety of factors, such as the initial fall in share prices, outright bond buying by the Finance Ministry and an accommodative money market operation by the Bank of Japan, traders said.
Some traders said public funds bought medium-term JGBs in the morning session.
"There was talk that public funds bought JGBs with five- to six-year maturities just around when (JGB futures) trade opened this morning," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Some said public funds sold two-year JGBs for five-year JGBs in order to reshuffle their portfolios.

"Public funds have been doing as they please in the market recently. They were detected buying after the release of the BOJ's tankan survey, and they have sold 10-year JGBs and also bought medium-term bonds," a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
The rise in JGBs in the morning session was tempered by selling of 10-year cash bonds, traders said.
"There was talk that a life insurer had sold some JGBs among the 190th to 197th issues," the third trader said.
Traders said they expected JGBs to remain firm, at least over the near term.

"After the release of the BOJ's tankan, industrial output and unemployment data the market has come to believe that a near-term rise in interest rates is unlikely," the analyst for a major brokerage house said.
JGBs have been firm recently, beyond the expectations of most dealers, a senior trust bank trader said.

"Dealers are feeling blue. They have been hurt because JGBs have been stronger than they had expected. Dealers were saying earlier they felt the upside of the September would be capped at 124.20," the trader said.
